facts.fact: The Internet Society Pulse IXP Tracker lists HubSIX, an exchange point in Dakar, with 6 member ASNs in PeeringDB, 5 of 6 peering at the route server, and 260 Gbps cumulative member port capacity (PeeringDB self-declared data, September 2026).

Two of the six HubSIX members in Dakar are registered in the United States (PCH AS3856 and PCH AS42), so networks from another country peer at the exchange, per PeeringDB data shown by Internet Society Pulse.

note: No traffic figure (capacity is port speed, not traffic); 6 new ASNs in 12 months is membership, not traffic growth; no content network among members.
Provisional forum programme only; names HubSIX and SENIX as technical supporters but does not state either is operating, no members, traffic or cities beyond the Dakar venue.
States only that a SENUM-Sonatel agreement of 25 March 2025 includes reactivating SENIX; no statement that it is in service or closed.
Regional Starlink article; exchange points named are in South Africa, Kenya and Nigeria, none in Senegal.

facts.fact: HubSIX says that in the week of 14 May 2026 the new Senegalese internet exchange point exceeded 2 Gbps of locally exchanged traffic for the first time, with operators, ISPs and CDNs as members.

note: No exchange point in this country stated.

facts.fact: The African IXP Association's undated list of exchange points, retrieved 2026-11-09, names for Senegal: SENIX and HubSIX, both in Dakar.

note: Document says nothing on exchange points.

facts.fact: The author says Senegal's national Internet exchange point, launched in 2017, appears little used, citing little public knowledge of its traffic.
